elements.initial_presentation: 62-year-old male presents to ED with severe, crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm and jaw for 90 minutes. Associated with diaphoresis, nausea, and shortness of breath. Vitals: BP 155/95 mmHg, HR 102 bpm, RR 22/min, SpO2 96% on room air.
elements.patient_history: History of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, 30 pack-year smoking. Medications: Amlodipine 5mg, Atorvastatin 20mg. No prior known CAD. NKDA.
elements.investigation_attachments: ECG: ST-segment elevation >2mm in leads II, III, and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL (Inferior STEMI). Initial Troponin I: 4.8 ng/mL (elevated).
